questions.text: Why do you want to study your chosen subject?
Tell me about something you have read or watched recently that changed how you think.
Describe a time you got something badly wrong. What did you do next?
What would you want to explore beyond your current syllabus, and why?
Explain something you find genuinely fascinating to someone who has never met the idea.
What is the most interesting question in your subject that nobody has fully answered yet?
Tell me about a piece of work you are proud of, and what made it good.
Describe a time you changed your mind about something important. What changed it?
What is a widely held opinion in your field of interest that you disagree with, and why?
Tell me about a book, article, or talk outside your school reading that shaped how you think about your subject.
Describe a time you had to work with someone whose approach was very different from yours. How did it go?
What would you do with an unplanned free afternoon and a good library?
Tell me about a time you had to explain something complicated to someone with no background in it.
What is something you used to find difficult that you have since got better at? How?
Describe a decision you made that you would make differently now.
What is a question you would like to ask an expert in your subject, and why that one?
Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teacher, tutor, or supervisor. How did you handle it?
What have you learned from a failure that you could not have learned any other way?
Describe something you built, wrote, organised, or solved outside the classroom.
What is a skill you have taught yourself, and how did you go about learning it?
Tell me about a time you had to persuade someone to see things your way.
What ethical question in your subject do you think about most, and where do you currently stand on it?
Describe a time you had to keep going with something difficult when you wanted to give up.
What is the difference between how your subject is taught at school and how you imagine it is actually practised?
Tell me about a time you worked as part of a team towards something you could not have done alone.
What would you change about how your subject is usually introduced to beginners?
Describe something you have made time for outside your studies that matters to you, and why.
What is a mistake commonly made by people new to your subject, and how would you avoid it?
Tell me about a piece of feedback that was hard to hear but useful.
If you could sit in on one lecture, seminar, or piece of research in progress this year, what would it be, and why?
